Mismatch.description: Three names for two values. There is no way to resolve that positionally without guessing which value was meant to be skipped, and guessing would silently misname a constant, so the whole extension is refused and every name is derived.

Duplicate.description: Two entries that identifierize to the same Go name would emit a redeclaration that does not compile. The later one is refused and derived instead.

NotAnIdentifier.description: Entries are author-supplied text, so they are identifierized rather than trusted; this keeps output compilable. A entry that yields nothing usable falls back to the derived name.

SelfNamed.description: A varname equal to its own enum's type name. Package.AddDecl dedupes by name and keeps the first declaration, so emitting this would drop the constant in silence rather than fail.

Shadowing.description: A supplied name equal to another entry's derived name. Every position falls back to its derived name, so this collides with whatever ends up using it, and AddDecl would drop one constant in silence.
